documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Regional hospital ED. Date of service 12/16/2025, arrival 22:10. Received by fax 1/14/2026.

CHIEF COMPLAINT: Hard to wake up.

HPI: 26-year-old woman with a history of generalized anxiety disorder, migraine and IBS-D, brought in by her roommate. Roommate came home and could not get her to wake up properly in bed; per roommate, patient may have swallowed a handful of pills earlier tonight after a recent breakup. Pill bottle at bedside was her own alprazolam 0.25 mg. History initially limited by mental status.

Home medications (per roommate and pharmacy): sertraline 50 mg daily, alprazolam 0.25 mg as needed (max 2/day), sumatriptan 50 mg as needed, ginger extract 500 mg as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: GAD, migraine without aura, IBS-D. PSH: wisdom teeth.
FH: mother GAD, father migraine, maternal grandmother IBS.
SH: graduate student. Never smoker. Alcohol socially, 1-2 drinks a week.

EXAM ON ARRIVAL
Vitals: BP 106/64, HR 56, RR 10, SpO2 93% on room air.
General: somnolent, opens eyes and responds to voice.
Neuro: speech slurred. Ataxic when tested. Pupils 3 mm, equal, reactive. Moves all extremities.
HEENT: no head trauma. No tongue laceration.
CV: bradycardic, regular, no murmur.
Resp: shallow respirations, clear bilaterally.
Abd: soft, nontender.
Skin: no track marks, no wounds.

ED COURSE
Placed on monitor and continuous pulse oximetry. Naloxone given IV with no change in mental status. Flumazenil given IV; within minutes she became noticeably more alert. No seizure activity during the stay. Observed overnight on monitor. Repeat vitals at 02:15: BP 112/70, HR 68, RR 14, SpO2 98% on room air. Ambulating steadily by morning.

Once awake, patient states she took most of what was left in her alprazolam bottle late in the evening, unsure of the count, perhaps 10-15 tablets, after a breakup. Says she wanted to sleep and shut everything off. Denies wanting to die. Denies prior ingestions or self-harm. Denies current suicidal thoughts. No other substances.

RESULTS
BMP within normal limits. Acetaminophen <10, salicylate <3.0, ethanol <10 (all undetectable). Urine drug screen positive for benzodiazepines; opiates negative. Urine hCG negative.
ECG: sinus bradycardia 56, normal intervals, no ST changes.

BEHAVIORAL HEALTH
Evaluated in the ED by the behavioral health team in the morning. Judged safe for discharge with a safety plan. No firearms at home. Roommate present, agrees to stay with her and to remove the remaining tablets from the apartment.

IMPRESSION
Benzodiazepine overdose (own alprazolam), intent undetermined. Resolved CNS and respiratory depression.

DISPOSITION
Discharged home with roommate 12/17/2025 09:30.
- Stop alprazolam.
- Continue sertraline.
- Follow up with primary care within the week.
- Outpatient counseling; crisis line and 988 information given.
- Return for any thoughts of self-harm.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I wanted you to hear this from me. I was in the ER last night. I took too many of my Xanax after my boyfriend and I broke up, my roommate found me and drove me in. They kept me overnight and let me go this morning. They said to see you this week. I'm ok, embarrassed mostly. My roommate is staying with me.

documents.title: RE: ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hannah, thank you for telling me, and I'm glad you're safe and not alone. I've asked the front desk to call you for Friday morning. Until then, please don't take any of the alprazolam, and if things get bad at any point, call me, call 988, or go back to the ER. We'll go through everything Friday.

orders.reason: Generalized anxiety disorder; follow-up after benzodiazepine overdose

documents.title: Office Visit - ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED FOLLOW-UP

Seen 3 days after an outside ED visit for an overdose of her own alprazolam. ED records not here yet, requested today. History from Hannah.

Tuesday night, after a breakup earlier that week, she took most of the remaining alprazolam from her last fill (thinks 10-15 tabs). Says she wanted to sleep and not feel anything. Did not want to die, and she is clear and consistent about that. Roommate found her and brought her in. She remembers waking in the ED and being told the reversal medicine worked. Kept overnight, seen by their behavioral health team, sent home Wednesday morning with a safety plan. No prior ingestions or self-harm. No alcohol or other pills that night.

Since: sleeping poorly, crying some, anxious, but going to campus. Roommate is staying close. Remaining alprazolam was thrown out. No firearms. Denies current SI, intent or plan. Taking sertraline daily.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Tired-appearing, cooperative, tearful at times, linear thought, good eye contact. Speech normal. Gait steady. Neuro nonfocal.

GAD-7 13, PHQ-9 7 (item 9 = 0).

A/P
1. Benzodiazepine overdose, 12/16, medically recovered. Alprazolam stopped and removed from her list; not refilling, discussed why. Reviewed the ED safety plan together, she has it on her phone. Crisis numbers reviewed.
2. GAD, more active with the stress. Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Referral to behavioral health for therapy; she is willing and wants someone she can see weekly. 
3. Will call her early January, visit in about 6-8 weeks, sooner if needed. She knows she can text me.

Spent 40 minutes, more than half counseling.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed records request to regional hospital ED for 12/16-12/17/2025 visit, signed release attached. Asked for ED physician record and behavioral health evaluation.

documents.title: Check-in call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Hannah as planned. Got through the holidays with family, back in her apartment now. Sleeping better. No thoughts of harming herself. Has an intake with a therapist from the referral list on the 13th. Not missing the alprazolam much, uses the breathing exercises instead. Taking sertraline. Will see me in February. ED records still not received, front desk to resend.

documents.title: Outside ED record reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED physician record from 12/16 finally arrived after the second request. Reviewed. Consistent with what she told me: own alprazolam, flumazenil response, tox screen otherwise negative, normal BMP, ECG sinus brady with normal intervals, observed overnight and discharged after their behavioral health eval. Their separate behavioral health note was not included; will not chase further unless needed. Nothing changes in the plan.

documents.title: Therapy
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just an update - I started seeing a therapist, weekly on Tuesdays. Two sessions so far and I like her. Thanks for pushing me on this.

documents.title: RE: Therapy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great news. Glad it's a good fit. See you in February.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, about 8 weeks after the December ED visit.

Feels steadier. Weekly therapy since January, working on anxiety skills and the breakup. Sleeping 6-7 hours. Back to her writing schedule. No thoughts of self-harm since December, none now. No alcohol binges, still 1-2 drinks a week. Has not wanted the alprazolam back. Sertraline daily.
IBS-D: a rough week in December, quiet since. Migraine: 2 in January, sumatriptan worked.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well groomed, brighter affect, at ease. Normal speech and thought process.

GAD-7 9, PHQ-9 4.

A/P
1. Overdose in December, resolved; off alprazolam and staying off. Safety plan still in place.
2. GAD improving with therapy plus sertraline 50 mg. Continue.
3. IBS-D, migraine stable.
Video check-in in 3 months.

Video from her apartment, identity confirmed.

Doing well. Still in weekly therapy, may go every other week over the summer. Anxiety close to her old baseline. No SI. Gut fine on her usual diet. Migraines 1-2/month.

GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 3.

Plan: continue sertraline 50 mg daily, sumatriptan as needed, therapy. Physical in the fall.
